name: Henry Debosnys's four cryptograms, Essex County jail, New York, 1882-83
ciphertext_pending: Cryptogram 1 (six lines in a simple-symbol alphabet) and three more; images in Cheri Farnsworth, The Adirondack Enigma (2010) and on Cipherbrain post 3 (2020; image URLs in sources/schmeh/posts/03-debosnys.html, not fetched); partial transcriptions on Cipher Mysteries and in Bauer, Unsolved! (2017). Originals at the Adirondack History Center Museum, Elizabethtown NY (which also holds his skull and his clear-text poems and drawings).
alphabet: simple invented symbols; count per cryptogram to be established

constraints.author: French-speaking, claimed Portuguese birth, wrote poems in French and English in the same papers, educated (Latin, Greek)
constraints.host_text: his clear poems from the same jail papers are the natural crib and form source: line counts and lengths of the cryptograms vs his clear verse
constraints.attempts: few (Schmeh 2020: 'only few crypto experts have occupied themselves')

cheap_tests_in_order: 1. Fetch the four images once (Schmeh's post, 4 requests, or Farnsworth's scans as cited) and transcribe in two passes; symbol counts, IC, line structure. Cost $4, Sonnet.

2. Form test (Urquhart lesson b): compare the cryptograms' line and syllable counts with his clear poems; if a cryptogram has the shape of a poem he also wrote in clear, the clear poem is a full crib. Cost $1.

3. Homophonic/MASC anneal in fr, en, pt, la with a control at each cryptogram's N and K (tools/homophonic_anneal.py, corpora fr16/it16/en on disk; Portuguese to be fetched). Cost $4, Sonnet; strongest model to read the result against his biography.
4. Archive: the museum's holdings list for a key sheet among his papers (an ASKS row; a cheap email).
matched_control: same N and K, French plaintext (fr16), same solver

judge.note: fr16 is 16th-century French; a 19th-century French corpus should be added before judging

value: high: Schmeh's no. 3, a documented author with clear-text siblings, few prior attempts
model: Sonnet for 1-3, strongest model for the reading
status_24_Sept_2026: open; no solution found 24 Sept 2026 (web search, Wikipedia list of ciphertexts, Bourdeau's excluded list)
schema_note: cheap_tests_in_order are proposals (rule 10: an approach is not a claim); a test actually run is under cheap_test_done with its control
